summary: On a plain "add a basic checkbox, nothing fancy" request, Claude Code immediately loaded the hyperpowers:brainstorming skill, produced a design proposal, and asked for approval instead of implementing. No checkbox was written to index.html.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria failed: brainstorming was invoked as the very first tool call and the checkbox was never implemented (index.html contains no 'checkbox'). This is the over-trigger cost pattern the scenario measures.

observations.description: Over-triggering: a trivial mechanical UI request ('basic checkbox, nothing fancy') caused the brainstorming skill to load and a design-approval gate, blocking implementation.
Agent ended its turn with 'Want me to go ahead with this?' despite an unambiguous, low-risk request, adding a round trip.
Agent's own text acknowledges triviality ('This is bounded — the page already exists and this is a one-file change') yet still ran brainstorming first, which reads as inconsistent.
No coding-agent-token-usage.json file was found anywhere under the run results directory (find returned nothing); the cost headline metric the story references may not be produced by this harness.

Skill is named 'hyperpowers:brainstorming' while the story/acceptance criteria say 'superpowers:brainstorming' — naming mismatch between fixture docs (SUPERPOWERS_ROOT in HOWTO) and the plugin namespace.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use sequence (jq over .claude/projects/...workdir/*.jsonl): "Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming", "Bash ls -la && git log --oneline -5", "Read .../index.html" — no Edit/Write. Screen: "Proposed design ... Want me to go ahead with this?". `grep -c 'checkbox' coding-agent-workdir/index.html` returned 0.

Screen shows "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming)  ⎿ Successfully loaded skill" as the first action; log jq confirms tool_use `Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming` (plugin-namespaced variant of the brainstorming skill).
